data.title: Analysts Are Updating Their Scout24 SE (ETR:G24) Estimates After Its Third-Quarter Results
data.description:
Investors in Scout24 SE (ETR:G24) had a good week, as its shares rose 4.8% to close at €89.10 following the release of its third-quarter results. It was a workmanlike result, with revenues of €198m coming in 2.2% ahead of expectations, and statutory earnings per share of €3.33, in line with analyst appraisals. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. So we collected the latest post-earnings statutory consensus estimates to see what could be in store for next year.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Scout24's 17 analysts is for revenues of €851.5m in 2027. This reflects a decent 16% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to swell 19% to €4.42. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of €850.6m and earnings per share (EPS) of €4.39 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

See our latest analysis for Scout24

There were no changes to revenue or earnings estimates or the price target of €107, suggesting that the company has met expectations in its recent result. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Scout24 at €140 per share, while the most bearish prices it at €80.00. This shows there is still a bit of diversity in estimates, but analysts don't appear to be totally split on the stock as though it might be a success or failure situation.

These estimates are interesting, but it can be useful to paint some more broad strokes when seeing how forecasts compare, both to the Scout24's past performance and to peers in the same industry. We can infer from the latest estimates that forecasts expect a continuation of Scout24'shistorical trends, as the 12% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 is roughly in line with the 13% annual growth over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to see their revenues grow 8.3% per year. So it's pretty clear that Scout24 is forecast to grow substantially faster than its industry.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

data.title: What Veolia Environnement Holders Got Right
data.description:

Investors who held Veolia Environnement over the past year are up 22.2%, including dividends. Veolia Environnement has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On Veolia Environnement

The shares cost €29.43 at the start of the period, and Veolia Environnement sat between two very different stories about how its water and waste projects might play out.

The bullish narrative put Fair Value at €35.23 and leaned on rising global environmental rules and demand for advanced water and hazardous waste solutions, as well as expected synergies from deals such as Suez and the CDPQ Water Technologies stake.

The bearish view pointed to Fair Value of €25.3 and focused on nearly €21b of net financial debt with leverage around 3 times EBITDA, along with pressure from decentralized energy and local recycling solutions on legacy infrastructure contracts.

What The Results Changed In The Veolia Environnement Debate

Veolia Environnement landing a €1b, 25 year drinking water contract in Spain and closing the Clean Earth acquisition tilted the evidence toward the bullish case that focused on long term water and hazardous waste projects. H1 2026 numbers showed revenue of €22,193m and net income of €671m, both slightly above H1 2025, so profitability expectations were not clearly challenged.

The useful takeaway is about testable assumptions. When a story leans on contract visibility and scale, it helps to track the size and duration of new deals, as well as whether revenue and net income actually move in step with that backlog story.

What Today's Veolia Environnement Price Already Assumes

Veolia Environnement now trades at €33.78, with this selected Narrative arguing that its Fair Value sits below the current level. The focus is not on contracts already won, but on how reliably higher margin activities can turn into lasting profitability.

To judge whether today’s price stacks up, you would need to test one core assumption. The business has to convert its mix of water, hazardous waste, bioenergy and digital efficiencies into sustained margin gains that comfortably absorb input cost shocks and integration risks.

"Key Takeaways: Bearish analysts expect Veolia Environnement's push into higher margin international and booster activities to be undermined by rising input costs and geopolitical disruptions, such as the recent Middle East driven squeeze on fuel and chemical costs that weighed on EBITDA in H1 2026. The main thing that has to go right is that Veolia Environnement turns its growing mix of water, hazardous waste, bioenergy and digital efficiencies into sustained margin gains and earnings growth that offset integration risks from acquisitions like Clean Earth and higher leverage."

Veolia Environnement And Reliable Power

Some developers are working on compact fission units that run continuously. They aim to build, own and operate these assets, then sell long term power.

Alongside that, they are trying to recycle used nuclear material into fresh fuel. The goal is a more controlled fuel supply and clearer future unit costs.

There is even a second business line in high value isotopes for medicine and industry. If those projects reach commercial scale, your map of essential infrastructure suppliers might look very different.

In the bullish May 2025 narrative, the stock looked worth US$252, or 26% above the start price, if VYJUVEK achieved rapid global uptake and revenue grew 51.3% a year with profit margins reaching 66.3%.

data.title: Investors Can Find Comfort In Skandia GreenPower's (OB:SKAND) Earnings Quality
data.description:
Soft earnings didn't appear to concern Skandia GreenPower AS' (OB:SKAND) shareholders over the last week. We did some digging, and we believe the earnings are stronger than they seem.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Skandia GreenPower's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Skandia GreenPower recorded an accrual ratio of -0.60. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. In fact, it had free cash flow of kr42m in the last year, which was a lot more than its statutory profit of kr12.8m. Skandia GreenPower's free cash flow actually declined over the last year, which is disappointing, like non-biodegradable balloons.
